newsitem.title: USA: GE earnings up 11 percent; sees record results for year.
newsitem.headline: GE earnings up 11 percent; sees record results for year.

text.p: General Electric Co. said Thursday its earnings rose 11 percent to a record in the first-quarter and that it was in a position to deliver record results for the entire year.

The company, whose interests range from aircraft engines to the NBC television network, said it earned $1.67 billion, or $1.02 a share, on revenues of $20.15 billion. That compared with year-earlier profits of $1.51 billion, or 91 cents a share, on revenues of $17.09 billion.
GE said 10 of its 12 businesses reported higher operating profit for the first quarter, with six, led by GE Capital Services, Power Systems and Aircraft Engines, achieving double-digit increases.
GE Capital Services' earnings were $754 million, 16 percent higher than last year's $650 million, boosted by the globalization and diversity of its businesses.
The results were led by strong double-digit increases in specialised financing, speciality insurance and equipment management activities, the Fairfield, Conn., conglomerate said.

"These strong first-quarter results position GE to deliver another year of record performance in 1997," said Chairman John Welch. "During the quarter, GE's expansion into services accelerated," he said.

GE said NBC won its ninth consecutive ratings sweep and moved its MSNBC cable TV and Internet news operation into a new state-of-the-art studio during the quarter. MSNBC is a joint venture with Microsoft Corp.
GE Capital continued its insurance growth with the acquisition of Coregis, Xerox's property and casualty insurance business.
GE Information Services expanded its Internet activities with a joint venture with Thomas Publishing and a new venture with Internet software company Netscape Communications Corp.
GE's equipment service businesses continued their rapid expansion as Power Systems closed long-term service agreements valued at $700 million, GE said.

its Aircraft Engines division announced an agreement to acquire Greenwich Air Services and UNC Inc., with joint revenues of $1.8 billion, to expand its service capabilities. Aircraft Engines also won more than 60 percent of the orders for large commercial engines during the quarter.
Recent Delta Air Lines' orders alone totalled $1.3 billion for engines to power 101 Boeing 737 and 767 aircraft, GE said.
As part of its $13 billion share repurchase programme, GE purchased $843 million of its stock during the first quarter to reach $7.3 billion.
GE's stock fell 50 cents to $101.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
